content: 1. Cefuroxime Dosage Guidelines: For patients older than 12 years: Administer 250-500 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. For children aged 3 months to 12 years: Administer 30 mg/kg/day orally in divided doses every 12 hours for 10 days, not exceeding 1000 mg/day. Alternatively, administer 75-150 mg/kg/day intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) in divided doses every 8 hours, not exceeding 6 g/day. For infants younger than 3 months: Safety and efficacy have not been established. For neonates under 6 days old and weighing less than 2 kg: Administer 100 mg/kg/day IV or IM in divided doses every 12 hours. For neonates under 6 days old and weighing more than 2 kg: Administer 150 mg/kg/day IV or IM in divided doses every 8 hours. For neonates older than 7 days: Administer 150 mg/kg/day IV or IM in divided doses every 8 hours. 2. Drug Interactions: BCG Vaccine (Live): Cefuroxime reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. This interaction is contraindicated. Cholera Vaccine: Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine within 14 days of oral or parenteral antibiotic use. Microbiota Oral Supplements: Antibiotics like cefuroxime may reduce the efficacy of microbiota oral supplements by decreasing bacterial spore activity. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. Aluminum Hydroxide: This antacid increases gastric pH, reducing cefuroxime absorption and efficacy. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use with caution and monitor closely. Amikacin: Cefuroxime increases the nephrotoxic and ototoxic effects of amikacin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use with caution and monitor renal function. Atezolizumab, Avelumab, Balstilimab, Camrelizumab, Cemiplimab, Durvalumab, Nivolumab, Pembrolizumab, Retifanlimab, Sintilimab, Tislelizumab, Toripalimab: Cefuroxime may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified mechanism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, Doxycycline, Erythromycin (all forms), Minocycline, Tetracycline: These bacteriostatic agents may antagonize the bactericidal effects of cefuroxime. Use with caution and monitor for reduced efficacy. Calcium Carbonate, Cimetidine, Esomeprazole, Famotidine, Omeprazole, Rabeprazole, Sodium Bicarbonate, Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate: These agents increase gastric pH, reducing cefuroxime absorption and efficacy. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Administer cefuroxime at least 2 hours before or after these agents. Chloramphenicol: This bacteriostatic agent may reduce the bactericidal effects of cefuroxime. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate, Ethinyl Estradiol, Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Bisglycinate: Cefuroxime may alter intestinal flora, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but additional contraceptive methods may be advisable. Furosemide: Cefuroxime may increase the nephrotoxic effects of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor renal function closely. Gentamicin, Kanamycin, Neomycin, Plazomicin, Streptomycin, Tobramycin: Cefuroxime increases the nephrotoxic and ototoxic effects of these aminoglycosides. Use with caution and monitor renal function. Probenecid: This agent increases cefuroxime levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use with caution and monitor for increased drug levels. Rose Hips: May increase cefuroxime levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Antibiotics like cefuroxime may reduce the efficacy of this combination by altering colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. Use with caution and monitor closely. Voclosporin: Co-administration with cefuroxime may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor renal function closely. Warfarin: Cefuroxime may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Use with caution and monitor coagulation parameters. 3. Special Considerations: Antibiotics, including cefuroxime, may reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines and hormonal contraceptives. Patients should be advised to use alternative or additional contraceptive methods during antibiotic therapy. Monitor renal function closely when cefuroxime is co-administered with nephrotoxic agents, such as aminoglycosides or diuretics. For drugs with pH-dependent solubility, administer cefuroxime at least 2 hours before or after agents that increase gastric pH.
